message.content:
**ServiceNow, Inc. (CIK 1373715) — operating expense profile, FY2022–FY2024**

ServiceNow's operating expenses grew in absolute dollars but fell steadily as a share of revenue, so the expense profile shifted toward operating leverage over the three-year period. All figures are full-year (10-K, fiscal years ended December 31), in USD.

**Total operating expenses** (GAAP, `OperatingExpenses`):
- FY2022: $5,317M (fact 1345337, accession 0001373715-25-000010)
- FY2023: $6,288M (fact 1345349, same accession)
- FY2024: $7,333M (fact 1345358, same accession)

Total opex rose 16.6% in FY2024 (calculated from $7,333M / $6,288M − 1), while revenue rose from $7,245M (FY2022) to $8,971M (FY2023) to $10,984M (FY2024) (facts 1349396, 1349408, 1349417). As a result, total opex as a percentage of revenue declined from 73.4% (FY2022) to 70.1% (FY2023) to 66.8% (FY2024) — a 6.6 percentage-point improvement over two years (calculated).

**Functional mix as % of revenue** (calculated from the line-item facts):

| Line | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sales & marketing | 38.8% | 36.8% | 35.1% |
| Research & development | 24.4% | 23.7% | 23.2% |
| General & administrative | 10.1% | 9.6% | 8.5% |
| Cost of revenues | 21.7% | 21.4% | 20.8% |

Dollar amounts: S&M $2,814M → $3,301M → $3,854M; R&D $1,768M → $2,124M → $2,543M; G&A $735M → $863M → $936M; cost of revenues $1,573M → $1,921M → $2,287M (facts 1349876/1349888/1349897, 1349108/1349120/1349129, 1341216/1341228/1341237, 1338234/1338246/1338255).

**What drove it (management's explanation, FY2024 10-K):** S&M rose $553M (+17%), mainly headcount-driven personnel costs (+$330M), higher deferred-commission amortization (+$90M) and program/branding spend (+$95M); R&D rose $419M (+20%), mainly personnel costs (+$350M) and outside services (+$48M); G&A rose $73M (+8%), mainly personnel costs (+$37M) and other corporate/outside services (+$67M), partly offset by a $36M stock-based compensation decrease (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:188800, :190400, :192000). Stock-based compensation rose to $1,746M but fell to 16% of revenue from 18% (chunk :193600).

**Interpretation:** the profile is one of scale leverage — every major function grew in dollars, but each declined as a percentage of revenue, with G&A showing the largest proportional decline and R&D the smallest. Management guided FY2025 expenses to keep rising in absolute dollars while staying roughly flat or slightly lower as a percentage of revenue. Note that these are GAAP figures including stock-based compensation; no non-GAAP expense ratios were reconstructed.
